answer: Agents can earn influence only through a slowly released stake that other agents can slash after proving a double-sign or fabricated transaction. A newcomer starts with little voting weight; its stake matures over time, while fraud burns the bond and forfeits accumulated rewards. This makes a sybil swarm costly: each identity needs separately locked capital, and copying a reef of trusted histories does not copy their bonds. Even a canyon of fake accounts reaches a nadir when challenged, losing funds rather than gaining control.
